clues.text: While working under Eugen Bleuler (“OY-gen BLOY-ler”) at a schizophrenia hospital, this man developed his concept of a “feeling-toned complex” after conducting his “word association” experiment.

This man posited that “people who would have never thought that a religious problem could be a serious matter … are beginning to ask themselves fundamental questions” in his book Flying Saucers: A Modern Myth of Things Seen in the Skies.
This thinker argued that an individual’s psychological change from an impure soul to a perfected soul is a parallel to transforming lead into gold in his work Psychology and Alchemy.
One concept developed by this man describes events with no causal connection that seem meaningfully related.
This man described his creative method of “active imagination” in his Red Book, and he examined the relationship between coincidences in his work Synchronicity.
He identified the “eternal child” and “wise old man” as shadow archetypes (“AHR-ki-types”), a term he also used to describe the animus and anima in his theory of the collective unconscious.
This psychologist developed the idea of the “shadow,” “anima,” and “persona,” and the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator is based off of this man’s research on introversion, extroversion, and archetypes.
This author of Psychological Types differentiated between “introversion” and “extraversion” and created the idea of the collective unconscious.
The Myers-Briggs Type Indicator was inspired by the work of what colleague of Sigmund Freud, a Swiss psychologist who developed the ideas of the collective unconscious and archetypes?
Name this Swiss founder of analytic psychology who once studied under Sigmund Freud.

clues.text: Durable goods in this type of structure have theoretically competitive prices according to the Coase conjecture.
Maximizing social welfare under this situation is the subject of the Ramsey problem.
The Pacman and Coase conjectures offer differing predictions of elements of this situation.
Price competition may be governed by the Coase conjecture in this economic system.
A “natural” type of this situation may emerge due to economies of scale.
Deadweight loss is one result of this situation which occurs when prices are set higher to maximize profits, leading to a decline in production.
Increasing returns to scale create the “natural” type of this market structure.
Market inefficiencies result from this economic situation because firms will produce less output than they would in a competitive market.
Name this market structure in which a single supplier controls most or all of the market for a particular commodity.
Name this situation in which a product is entirely produced by one company.
One of this man's books claims that long-run expectations could not be quantified and were driven more by "animal spirits" than rational weighing of risks.
Some believe this author’s Indian Currency and Finance to be the greatest work written about the gold standard.
One mathematical model based on this man's most influential book explains shifts in aggregate demand and was developed by Hicks and Hansen.
This man argued that the long-term economy was driven by irrational human drives he termed “animal spirits.”

This man criticized some economists’ use of the “long run” by saying “in the long run, we’re all dead,” and he claimed that the terms set forth by the Treaty of Versailles were disastrous in his The Economic Consequences of the Peace.
His book The Means to Prosperity attacked Say’s law.

This economist names a "cross" diagram showing the relationship between aggregate demand and aggregate supply, and this theorist of the "money multiplier" attacked the terms of the Treaty of Versailles in The Economic Consequences of the Peace.
He is also known for his Tract on Monetary Reform, where he declared “In the long run, we are all dead.”
He also argued against high reparation payments for Germany in his The Economic Consequences of the Peace.
Name this economist who advocated deficit spending to combat recessions in The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money.
